wave_classification_reasons: vol_ratio_rank_20 (cross-sectional percentile rank of current-day volume relative to its own trailing 20-day average volume) has never been used as a ranking/classifier feature in any prior MiniQuantDesk experiment (ALPHA-01 used momentum_score, SHORT-01 used slope_60, SHORT-WAVE-02/03 used ret_rank_20/ret_5/gap_pct_1, DISCOVERY-01 used vol_rank_20, WAVE06 LIQ-01 uses illiquidity_amihud_rank_20) -- it is a genuinely untested, attention/visibility-based mechanism with no definitional overlap with any previously tested return, price-level, volatility, or illiquidity-level statistic

the economic rationale (investor-attention / high-volume return premium) is grounded in primary peer-reviewed literature, not retuned from an observed result: Gervais, Kaniel & Mingelgrin (2001), 'The High-Volume Return Premium', Journal of Finance 56(3):877-919; Barber & Odean (2008), 'All That Glitters: The Effect of Attention and News on the Buying Behavior of Individual and Institutional Investors', Review of Financial Studies 21(2):785-818

vol_ratio_rank_20 is definitionally distinct from LIQ-01's illiquidity_amihud_rank_20: illiquidity_amihud is a LEVEL statistic (price impact per dollar traded, i.e. |return|/dollar_volume, a cross-sectional and time-varying illiquidity COST), while vol_ratio is a temporally-RELATIVE own-history statistic (today's volume divided by that SAME symbol's trailing 20-day average volume, a volume SURPRISE/demand-shock signal) -- both happen to use volume data, but they measure different economic constructs (a compensation-for-trading-cost risk premium vs. an attention-driven demand shock) and are evaluated as two separately falsifiable candidates in this campaign, never conflated

the underlying vol_ratio statistic is NOT new code -- it is already unconditionally computed (unranked) by the existing, unmodified mqk_research.features.feature_set_v1.build_feature_set_v1; only the cross-sectional rank transform (identical formula to that same module's own vol_rank_20/atr_rank_14 ranking, applied locally in run_wave.py) is new, and it is a mechanical transform, not new statistical methodology

the seed universe reused here is the SAME current-registry, non-point-in-time 88-symbol snapshot used by SHORT-WAVE-03, DISCOVERY-01, and WAVE06 LIQ-01 (see docs/research/BROAD_RESEARCH_UNIVERSE_CURRENT_TRUTH_AUDIT.md) -- carrying the identical survivorship-bias caveat forward unchanged, not a fresh point-in-time-clean universe, and kept identical across this campaign's candidates so the only varying factor between LIQ-01 and VOL-01 is the feature itself

VOL-01.name: single-feature OOS classifier-score cross-sectional rank, high-volume/attention return premium predictor
primary_references: Gervais, Kaniel & Mingelgrin (2001), 'The High-Volume Return Premium', Journal of Finance 56(3):877-919
Barber & Odean (2008), 'All That Glitters: The Effect of Attention and News on the Buying Behavior of Individual and Institutional Investors', Review of Financial Studies 21(2):785-818
VOL-01.economic_rationale: A stock trading at unusually high volume relative to its own recent history draws disproportionate investor attention (the 'visibility hypothesis'); attention-driven buying pressure from investors who otherwise only choose among a small attention-constrained set of names has been documented to produce a subsequent short-horizon return premium. The classifier's OOS score is trained per fold using vol_ratio_rank_20 as its sole input feature against the SAME fwd_ret>0 binary label used by every prior single-feature family in this repo; the fold-trained logistic regression learns the empirical sign of the volume-surprise/forward-return relationship from training data itself -- no direction is hand-asserted here.
VOL-01.falsification_condition: REJECTED_NOT_ADVANCED if the candidate's risk-adjusted economic performance does not exceed the matched placebo by a non-negligible margin, and/or the candidate materially underperforms the dynamic rankable benchmark, and/or the long-short candidate does not meaningfully outperform its own long-only control.

distinctness_from_prior_mechanisms: vol_ratio_rank_20 requires trading VOLUME data (a symbol's own current volume relative to its own trailing 20-day average volume) -- no previously tested feature (momentum_score, slope_60, ret_rank_20, ret_5, gap_pct_1, vol_rank_20) uses volume at all; every one of those is a pure price-return or price-level statistic. It is also distinct from this same campaign's LIQ-01 candidate (illiquidity_amihud_rank_20): LIQ-01 is a cross-sectional LEVEL statistic (price impact per dollar traded), while vol_ratio_rank_20 is a temporally-RELATIVE own-history statistic (today's volume vs. that symbol's own recent average) -- a demand-shock/attention signal, not a trading-cost/liquidity-risk signal. The economic mechanism (investor attention, Gervais-Kaniel-Mingelgrin 2001 / Barber-Odean 2008) is a fundamentally different behavioral/microstructure family from momentum/reversal, the low-volatility/leverage-constraint mechanism (DISCOVERY-01, REJECTED_NOT_ADVANCED), or the illiquidity risk-premium mechanism (this campaign's own LIQ-01). This is not a retuned parameter variant of any prior family -- it is not a different lookback, threshold, K, universe, or rebalance interval applied to a previously tested statistic.

benchmark.definition: At each economic decision date, equal-weight the SAME causally rankable symbol set available to this family at that date (RANKABLE_SET(T)) -- no future membership, no holdout. Fold-reset semantics identical to SHORT-WAVE-03's/DISCOVERY-01's/WAVE06 LIQ-01's build_dynamic_rankable_benchmark convention.
benchmark.implementation_status: Already implemented and previously exercised by SHORT-WAVE-03's run_01 and DISCOVERY-01's RISK-01 family (benchmark_type=dynamic_equal_weight_causally_rankable_fold_reset_v1); reused verbatim unchanged in this experiment's run_wave.py (build_dynamic_rankable_benchmark), not reimplemented, not invented after seeing returns.
